newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares plunges at noon on crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares plunges at noon on crackdown.

text.p: Shanghai's A and B share indices were sharply down at midday on Thursday after Beijing imposed new curbs on the trading of shares by state-owned companies, barring them from making "speculative" deals, brokers said.
The B index fell 3.346 points or 3.79 percent to 84.829 points on volume of 8.61 million shares worth $5.662 million.
The A index tumbled 102.473 points or 7.24 percent to 1,313.646 on turnover of 5.07 billion yuan.
The ban, following other measures to cool down the stock markets, has greatly weakened market sentiment, brokers said.
The Xinhua news agency announced the move after the market close on Wednesday.
"The news dampened market sentiment, triggering panic selling, which pulled the indices sharply down this morning," one broker said.
"The indices will fall further in the next few days due to heavy selling pressure," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 36 traded, with 33 down, one flat and two up.
Phoenix was the biggest loser on poor prospects, diving $0.016 or 10.00 percent to $0.144 on volume of 11,100 shares.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded stock on institutional liquidation selling, slumping $0.052 or 7.12 percent to $0.678 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
On the A share market, the SSE30 blue chip index slipped 246.857 points or 6.05 percent to 3,836.182 points.
China Textile Machinery was the biggest loser on institutional selling, plunging 0.72 yuan or 10.05 percent to 6.44 yuan on volume of 525,600 shares.
